children: The recent rise in the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield has been driven by the real term premium, rather than inflation expectations or rate expectations, Variant Perception says in a note. "This can be viewed as a 'normalization' where the real term premium is back in its post-GFC [Global Financial Crisis] range." Variant's fair value for the 10-year yield is in the range of 4.10% to 4.35%. "The gap is wide, but not unprecedented, we saw similar gaps close in 2023 and 2024," it says. The 10-year Tresaury yield closed at 4.782% on Friday.(emese.bartha@wsj.com)
